description: A four-panel composite of EBSD boundary maps (grain-boundary / misorientation line maps) for Fe–8% Al low-density steel deformed by torsion at 1000 °C and 0.1 s⁻¹, at four increasing strains. All four panels are the same modality and share identical annotation: a black-and-white base image overlaid with a network of thin black lines and thin red lines, a black scale bar labelled "500 µm" in the lower-left of each panel, and a black double-headed arrow along the bottom edge (plus a matching arrow at the top-left in (a)–(d)) marking the torsion/shear axis. Panel captions read "a. ε = 1", "b. ε = 2", "c. ε = 5", "d. ε = 25". In (a) at ε = 1 large elongated original grains dominate and the red line network is patchy, concentrated in bands. At ε = 2 (b) the red subgrain-boundary network becomes denser and starts to invade grain interiors. At ε = 5 (c) the structure is fine and fairly uniform, black and red boundaries intermingled. At ε = 25 (d) the map is a homogeneous fine equiaxed cell/grain network with the highest density of boundaries. The figure demonstrates progressive fragmentation of the original grains and continuous conversion of low-angle into high-angle boundaries with increasing strain.

subfigures.description: EBSD boundary map at ε = 1: large original grains elongated along the shear direction, with pioneer subgrain (red-line) networks concentrated in bands and near initial grain boundaries; 500 µm scale bar and double-headed shear arrow.
EBSD boundary map at ε = 2: original grains more elongated along the shear direction; the red-line subgrain network is denser and invades grain interiors; 500 µm scale bar and shear arrow.

EBSD boundary map at ε = 5: fine, fairly homogeneous structure in which black and red boundary networks are intermingled and initial grain boundaries are no longer distinguishable; 500 µm scale bar and shear arrow.
EBSD boundary map at ε = 25: uniform, equiaxed fine network of grain/cell boundaries with the highest boundary density of the four panels; 500 µm scale bar and shear arrow.

observations.observation: The figure contains four EBSD boundary maps labelled 'a. ε = 1', 'b. ε = 2', 'c. ε = 5' and 'd. ε = 25', i.e. one map per strain level.
Every panel carries a black scale bar labelled '500 µm' in its lower-left corner.

Two boundary populations are drawn in each map: a network of thin black lines and a network of thin red lines; the maps also contain a black double-headed arrow indicating the shear/torsion direction along the bottom and upper-left edges.
At ε = 1 the original grains are large and elongated in the shear direction, and red-line subgrain networks occur in discrete bands rather than uniformly.
At ε = 2 the red-line (subgrain) network is denser and extends into the interiors of the original grains compared with ε = 1.
At ε = 5 and ε = 25 the map becomes a fine, fairly uniform network of boundaries with no distinguishable large original grains.
The caption identifies the images as EBSD maps of samples deformed by torsion at 1000 °C and 0.1 s⁻¹.
The citing text states that in Fig. 1a the original grains are clearly visible and elongated in the shear direction, with subgrains forming preferentially close to serrated initial grain boundaries.
The citing text states that in Fig. 1b the original grains are more elongated along the shear direction and a network of subgrains progressively invades the interior of the original grains.

The citing text states that in Fig. 1c it becomes impossible to distinguish initial grain boundaries from recrystallized grain boundaries, so the structure is described as an aggregate of crystallites bounded partly by LABs and partly by HABs.

The citing text attributes the generation of high angle boundaries (HABs) inside original grains to continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX) and notes that fragmentation is selective, some grains being more fragmented than others.
No numeric values (boundary misorientation angles, grain sizes, volume fractions) are printed on any panel; only the strain labels and the 500 µm scale bars are annotated.

The group makes one argument across panels: increasing strain progressively replaces the coarse elongated original-grain structure with a homogeneous fine boundary network, illustrating the continuous transformation of low-angle subgrain boundaries into high-angle grain boundaries.

unreadable_items: No legend is present, so the assignment of the red line network to low angle boundaries (LABs) and the black line network to high angle boundaries (HABs) is inferred from the citing text and the standard EBSD convention, not printed on the figure
The base grey-scale/albedo channel of the EBSD maps is not explained by any on-figure label
